extracted.intended_audience: Vanderbilt career-development/K-award applicants, institutional administrators, and NIH grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A Facilities & Other Resources section for a Vanderbilt career-development/clinical research grant describing institutional cores, training programs, access rules, program requirements, evaluation endpoints, and mentorship resources available to the PD/PI and trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTSD program evaluation endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office for CTSD will use endpoints such as publication rates, grant success (particularly K to R conversion), diversity among the faculty, retention of Newman Society members in academic medicine on the tenure track, and investment costs per faculty member to evaluate the success of its programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These endpoints are the metrics by which CTSD measures program success and guide investment and training decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: VPSD/VCTRS program participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are required to work within the research space/program of the mentor to ensure a close supervisory relationship and eliminate the need for awardees to obtain their own supplies or equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring clinical department chair must commit to provide 75% research time during the duration of the award, provide support to the mentor's laboratory to support applicant activities, and identify space and resources to support the applicant's eventual emergence as independent once federal funding is secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: VPSD/VCTRS selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are selected on a competitive basis by a committee of Vanderbilt faculty who emphasize the quality of the mentor and his or her research environment, the training credentials of the applicant, and the quality of the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program leadership (Associate Dean) monitors progress of awardees and engages departmental leadership when needed; programs provide salary, didactic coursework funds, research support and travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newman Society membership expectations and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: All Newman Society members (K awardees or internal K12-supported trainees) are expected to have at least 75% protected time for research; members meet every 6 months with the Associate Dean to review career and mentorship plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet the 75% protected time requirement will result in withdrawal of institutional salary support or the K award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript and grant writing support
rubrics_metrics.description: CTSD provides a repository of successfully funded grants and an internal pre-review of grants by senior faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources are intended to improve grant competitiveness and manuscript quality for trainees and junior faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: REDCap access and security/compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: REDCap and REDCap Survey provide secure, web-based applications for data collection/management with full audit-trails in compliance with HIPAA security requirements; REDCap Survey is designed for studies where data are collected directly from the research participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REDCap is available only to investigators from Vanderbilt and Meharry Medical College, but investigators at other institutions may use it if they are part of a Vanderbilt project/group utilizing REDCap.

rubrics_metrics.name: BioVU (Vanderbilt DNA Databank) access and consent policy
rubrics_metrics.description: BioVU contains DNA samples linked to de-identified electronic medical records; the 'consent-to-treat' form includes an opt-out box for patients. Only Vanderbilt researchers can apply as principal investigators to use BioVU, though collaborators can be from other centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BioVU has been reviewed to meet ethical standards; access is institutionally restricted to Vanderbilt PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic Derivative (SD) data characteristics and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The SD is a de-identified database derived from Vanderbilt's EMR (altered to no longer closely resemble the original record) containing ~1.9 million records including narratives, diagnostic and procedural codes, reports, lab values, vital signs, and medication orders; it can be used stand-alone or with BioVU for genome-phenome analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SD is a major institutional research resource for observational and translational research; users must follow de-identification and data use policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: VICTR Studios structure and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Studios are structured, dynamic sessions bringing together relevant Vanderbilt faculty research experts (2-6 experienced faculty) to focus on a specific stage of research (hypothesis generation, study design, implementation, analysis and interpretation, translation, manuscript development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studios are intended to enhance research quality, foster practice advances, increase publications, and generate new hypotheses; Translation Studios focus on community health implications and dissemination opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: StarBRITE shared data infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: StarBRITE is an online central repository storing up-to-date study documents and project characteristics for Vanderbilt investigators and serves as a unified system for tracking research education, mentoring, conduct, collaboration, resource utilization, and productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to establish open channels for feedback/input from VICTR and to centralize project tracking and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot funding (VICTR) application and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot funding is available via expedited vouchers for up to $2,000 for acquiring/analyzing small amounts of data or manuscript preparation; the application is reviewed within 48 hours and funds are immediately accessible upon approval. Requests over $2,000 require a more in-depth application and committee review and can be made available in as little as 2-4 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited small awards facilitate rapid preliminary analyses or manuscript completion to support grant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Research Center (CRC) purpose and services
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRC provides resources needed by clinical and translational investigators (outpatient space, inpatient beds, laboratories, equipment and supplies) in an environment optimized for safety, comfort and convenience of patients/volunteers; it also serves as a teaching site and apprenticeship environment and offers weekly workshops on practical clinical research skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRC workshops cover topics such as Excel for medical research, Access queries, and sample size computation and are taught in interactive format with computer demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biostatistics support and clinic services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Biostatistics provides design/analysis expertise to increase research quality and is available to assist in grant proposal development (including K award development) and manuscript writing; vouchers for biostatistics help are available through VICTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily Biostatistics walk-in clinics are free to Vanderbilt Investigators, held Monday–Friday with themed topics, open to Vanderbilt and Meharry communities, mentors should attend with post-docs/students, and investigators should email biostat-clinic@list.vanderbilt.edu by 9am the day they wish to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biostatistics Collaboration Center (BCC) services and expertise levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The BCC is a core resource providing statistical collaborations across design, conduct, analysis, and publication with personnel ranging from bachelor/master-level biostatisticians to full professors; services include salaries, administrative costs, supplies, computing and IT support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ACCRE provides flexible high performance computing and high performance storage resources to support large-scale analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship structure and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Medicine and Division of Infectious Diseases place high importance on mentorship: standing weekly meetings with a primary mentor are expected; a mentoring committee composed of experienced investigators provides expertise in study design, health policy research, epidemiology, and biostatistics to improve chances for success as the trainee develops independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors should have complementary skills (e.g., policy, epidemiology, biostatistics, cohort expertise) and a track record of mentoring (e.g., prior trainees who obtained K/R awards) to strengthen career-development plans.
